title: RAYE Announces One-Night Orchestral Show at Royal Albert Hall
excerpt: RAYE will perform her second album in full with an orchestra at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23 for a one-night concert.
body:
RAYE will perform her second album in full with an orchestra at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23 for a one-night concert. Titled *THIS SYMPHONY MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, the show will bring *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* to the stage with the Heritage Orchestra, the Flames Collective choir and her band. It is not planned as a collection of orchestral versions of familiar singles. Every song is included, and the order matters: RAYE built the record around four seasons, moving through difficult moments toward a more hopeful ending.

The venue has a particular place in her live history. In 2023, she performed her debut album, *My 21st Century Blues*, there with a 50-piece orchestra and choir. The concert was filmed and became *Live at the Royal Albert Hall*, later nominated for Best Music Film at the 2026 Grammy Awards. She brought that symphonic format to London's O2 arena the following year. The new performance returns to the original setting, but this time the music comes from her second album.

To accompany the announcement, RAYE shared a new performance of "I Will Overcome." recorded at Abbey Road Studios with the London Symphony Orchestra. It is a separate studio performance, not a recording of the upcoming concert, and the musicians are different from those announced for the Hall. The song appears near the beginning of *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, following its opening introduction. Hearing it with a full orchestra provides the first concrete example of how the new material can work in this format.

[youtube:Iy2FoVeIUXs]

Released in March, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* already makes room for jazz, big-band arrangements, soul and orchestral passages. Its songs move between heartbreak, self-doubt and the work of getting through both, with the changing musical styles tracking that emotional arc. "I Will Overcome." is an early statement of that idea, while the closing track, "Fin.", brings the record to its conclusion. Performing the album straight through should preserve those connections better than a conventional concert set built around the best-known songs.

The booking comes after a year of larger shows. RAYE has toured the album across the UK, Europe and North America, including several sold-out nights at the O2, and is currently appearing as a guest on Bruno Mars' stadium tour. This Royal Albert Hall show will have a different focus: a single record performed with a choir and orchestra rather than a selection from across her catalog. The choice to perform every track in order leaves little room for the usual concert shortcuts, including skipping the album's quieter passages.

Her first performance at the Hall eventually reached listeners far beyond the venue through its concert film. No recording or broadcast of the new date was announced with the show, so the Abbey Road video is the one confirmed preview for anyone who cannot attend. The second album has already reached No. 1 in the UK, but the October concert is being planned around the songs as a complete work rather than their individual success. For now, hearing the full new arrangements is something reserved for the room itself.
